scenarios.title: Restore service
scenarios.headline: A release goes wrong. What happens next?
scenarios.state: Deployment v42 was released 4 minutes ago. HTTP 500 errors rose from 0.1% to 24%. Previous v41 was healthy. Rollback to v41 is available and database schema is backwards compatible.
scenarios.question: Which action best restores service now?

options.rollback: Roll back to healthy v41 and verify errors recover.
options.scale: Add more replicas of the failing v42.

scenarios.outcome: Simulation: the previous release is restored. Error rate returns to 0.1%. Now investigate the regression.
scenarios.wrongOutcome: Simulation paused: this action does not address the faulty release. Review the evidence before proceeding.

scenarios.title: Find the fix
scenarios.headline: Turn a failing test into a focused next step.
scenarios.state: Test fails with ValueError on timestamp 2026-09-28T10:00Z. parse_date only accepts timestamps ending +00:00. Input contract explicitly allows ISO timestamps ending Z.
scenarios.question: Which fix best matches the evidence?

options.parser: Normalize the supported Z suffix to +00:00 before parsing.

scenarios.outcome: Simulation: the parser now accepts the documented timestamp format. The patch is ready for verification.
scenarios.wrongOutcome: Simulation paused: the selected action leaves the documented parsing behavior unresolved.

scenarios.title: Verify before shipping
scenarios.headline: A patch is only the beginning.
scenarios.state: The parser fix is applied but no tests have been run. Release policy requires the regression test and full suite to pass before deployment.
scenarios.question: What should the agent do next?

options.test: Run the regression test and full suite.

scenarios.outcome: Simulation: verification is requested. A real agent would run the tests and inspect their results before releasing.
scenarios.wrongOutcome: Simulation paused: the selected action does not meet the stated release policy.

scenarios.title: Route a customer request
scenarios.headline: Test the boundaries. Keep the result honest.
scenarios.state: Customer message: I was charged twice for the same order yesterday. Please refund the duplicate payment.
scenarios.question: Which team should handle this request?

options.technical: Technical support: application errors and crashes.
options.sales: Sales: new purchases and product demonstrations.

scenarios.outcome: The model agrees with the scenario's billing label. This is one illustrative example, not an accuracy benchmark.
scenarios.wrongOutcome: The model disagrees with the scenario's billing label. This is a visible failure case: keep human review for unsupported task families.
